title: Edge and CDN in one screen
rememberThis: A CDN caches responses at edge Points of Presence (PoPs) near users — fewer round trips to your origin region.
CloudFront distribution = domain + origins + cache behaviors. Behaviors match path patterns; the default behavior is the fallback.
Cache key includes path, query string, and any forwarded headers/cookies you opt in — wrong key = wrong cache or leaks.
Lock S3 behind CloudFront with Origin Access Control (OAC); never make the bucket public for static sites.
Dynamic /api/* paths go to API Gateway or ALB with TTL 0 (or very short) and Authorization forwarded — do not cache authenticated responses by accident.
bullets: Prefer versioned asset URLs (app.v2.js) over mass invalidation — invalidation paths cost and propagate globally.
Origin Shield adds a regional mid-tier cache between edge and origin for hot objects.
CloudFront Functions run at viewer request/response; Lambda@Edge runs at four trigger points with more runtime.
Use AWS WAF on the distribution for bot control and geo blocking at the edge.
SPA fallback: custom error 403/404 → /index.html on the S3 default behavior.

rows.label: PoP
rows.value: Edge location that serves cached content to nearby users

rows.label: Origin
rows.value: Upstream source CloudFront fetches on cache miss (S3, ALB, API GW, custom)

rows.label: Cache behavior
rows.value: Path pattern + origin + TTL + forwarded headers/cookies/query

rows.label: OAC
rows.value: SigV4-signed S3 access from CloudFront only — replaces legacy OAI

rows.label: TTL
rows.value: How long edge keeps an object; min/default/max caps apply

rows.label: Invalidation
rows.value: Purge paths from all edge caches — use sparingly; version URLs instead
